suggestions.title: Apocalypse Now
suggestions.description: A U.S. Army captain is sent on a dangerous mission into Cambodia to assassinate a renegade colonel, descending into the heart of darkness during the Vietnam War. Francis Ford Coppola's hallucinatory, monumental war epic blends surreal imagery, haunting sound design, and career-defining performances by Martin Sheen and Marlon Brando. A singular, decades-in-the-making obsession that remains one of the most powerful and controversial films ever made.

suggestions.title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
suggestions.description: The adventures of Gustave H, a legendary concierge at a famous European hotel between the wars, and his loyal lobby boy Zero as they become entangled in a stolen-painting heist. Wes Anderson's meticulously crafted, visually enchanting caper is a bittersweet meditation on friendship and a lost era, featuring one of Ralph Fiennes' greatest comedic performances. Quirky, witty, and gorgeous — a perfect pick for something utterly distinct.

suggestions.title: Memento
suggestions.description: A man with short-term memory loss uses notes, photographs, and tattoos to hunt for his wife's murderer, telling the story in reverse chronological order. Christopher Nolan's breakout cerebral thriller — anchored by a stunning Guy Pearce performance — rewired the psychological-thriller genre with its ingenious backwards structure. A puzzle-box masterpiece that rewards every rewatch.
